newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols firm but action slow.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols firm but action slow.

text.p: Implied volatilities in U.S. Treasury bond options firmed slightly Monday, but trading was extremely thin ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday Thursday, traders said.
"Things are pretty quiet. There are just a few players busy," one trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) said.
At 1245 CST (1845 GMT), implied volatility for January T-bond futures options was at 9.74 percent, up 0.33 percentage point from Friday's U.S. close.
Implied volatility for the March contract was up 0.15 percentage point, at 9.90 percent, from Friday's U.S. close.

"Basically the reason you're seeing that (volatility rise) is because of the calendar we've got the rest of the week," a trader said. "Plus it's a shortened week, so you put those components in the mix and that's what you get."
The market will be closed on Thursday but traders are faced with a fairly heavy slate of economic data this week, including October durable goods and personal income and consumption.
November data scheduled for release include consumer sentiment and the Chicago purchasing managers' index.

Early Monday, the National Association of Realtors said sales of existing U.S. homes fell 1.5 percent in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.97 million units from a revised 4.03 million in September.
But traders said the data had little impact on activity.
"I can't remember a more quiet day," one dealer at the CBOT said, adding that few blocks of 1,000 contracts or more had crossed by midday.
He said some traders taking Friday's shortened session off could pump up volatilities through Wednesday to protect themselves from any sharp market move.
"Then on Monday it'll be all over and they'll crash back down," he said.
But others said volatility could remain high through next week because of the all-important employment report, due December 6.
"I think 10.5 volatility is something you might see in the March (contract) and possibly the January (contract) as well before we get to unemployment Friday," said one dealer.
"They'll be selling into it or buying into it and I think they'll be buying into it early and selling later in the week," he said.
Firm T-bond volatilities contrasted with flat implied volatilities for eurodollar futures options at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Implied volatilities for the March and June at-the-money contracts were flat, at 11 percent and 15.3 percent respectively, one trader at the CME said.
He said slow trading could persist until Japan's tankan business survey is released Tuesday at 2350 GMT.
"But the big one is the December 6 (U.S.) nonfarm payrolls report," he said. --Gregory Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com
